questions.question: What must you NOT do to a moving vehicle ahead of you inside crossing zig-zags?
options: Leave a two-second gap behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans overtaking any leading moving or stopped vehicle at a crossing.

questions.question: Why do busy crossroads have yellow box junctions?
options: To stop queuing cars from blocking crossing traffic
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps the centre of busy junctions clear for cross traffic.

questions.question: When passing a cyclist riding past parked cars, why leave extra room?
options: A parked car door could suddenly open into the cyclist's path
The cyclist must ride on the kerb
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 notes cyclists ride away from parked cars to avoid opening doors.

questions.question: What is the main danger of driving too close to the car in front?
options: You may not have time to stop if they brake suddenly
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 warns that tailgating leaves no room to stop safely.

questions.question: What should you do before signalling to pull over and stop?
options: Check your mirrors to see who is behind you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 works with mirror checks so others understand your signal.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car on a dual carriageway with a central barrier?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 70 mph for cars on dual carriageways unless signed lower.

questions.question: Which lights mean you must wait behind the stop line?
options: Red, steady amber (if safe to stop), and red with amber
questions.explain: Rule 175: all three phases require you to wait behind the stop line.

questions.question: As you approach a Give Way line, what should you do?
options: Slow down early so you can stop if traffic is coming
Keep your speed until the last metre
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 tells drivers to approach under control ready to give way.

questions.question: When a lane ahead is closed by cones, when should you merge?
options: Early and smoothly when you see a safe gap
At the very last cone by forcing in
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises changing lanes smoothly in good time.

questions.question: Does an entering car have priority over a car already on the roundabout?
options: No, traffic already on the roundabout from the right has priority
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 gives priority to circulating traffic from the right.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a roundabout?
options: Stay on and go clockwise all the way around again
Stop and reverse back to the exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says never reverse or turn back; simply go around clockwise.

questions.question: What do dashed white spiral lines on a large roundabout show?
options: Which lane path to follow to reach your exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide traffic smoothly around large roundabouts.

questions.question: When taking the third exit to the right at a two-lane roundabout, which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses the right-hand lane for exits to the right unless signed otherwise.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a triangular school warning sign ahead?
options: Slow down and watch carefully for children
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 208 warns you to drive slowly near schools and watch for children.

questions.question: What does a single steady amber light mean?
options: Speed up to beat the red
Stop behind the stop line unless unsafe to do so
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 175 says AMBER means stop at the stop line, unless you are so close that stopping might cause a collision.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a pedestrian waiting to cross at a zebra crossing?
options: Slow down and be ready to stop to give way
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 195 says you should look out for pedestrians waiting to cross and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why are children especially hard to spot near parked cars outside a school?
options: They are small and may step out suddenly
questions.explain: Rule 208: children are smaller than parked cars and can step into the road without warning.

questions.question: When may you pass a steady amber traffic light?
options: Whenever you are in a hurry
Only if you have crossed the line or cannot stop safely
questions.explain: Rule 175: you may only go on amber if stopping suddenly could cause a crash.

questions.question: What MUST you do once a pedestrian has moved onto a zebra crossing?
questions.explain: Rule 195 states you MUST give way when a pedestrian has moved onto a crossing.

questions.question: What MUST you do when a school crossing patrol holds up a red and yellow Stop sign?
options: Stop and wait until they lower the sign
Only stop if children are in your lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 210 says you MUST stop when signalled by a school crossing patrol.

questions.question: May a motorcycle stop inside a cyclist advanced stop box on red?
options: No, motor vehicles must stop behind the first white line
questions.explain: Rule 178: the ASL box is for pedal cyclists only.

questions.question: If the car ahead of you stops at a STOP line and moves off, what must you do when you reach the line?
options: Stop again at the white line yourself
questions.explain: Rule 171: every vehicle must stop at the line in turn and check both ways.

questions.question: What kind of road marking goes with a STOP sign?
options: A solid white line and STOP painted on the road
questions.explain: Rule 171: a STOP sign is paired with a solid white stop line across your lane.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction, and the road you want to turn into is jammed full. May you enter the box?
options: No, because your exit road is blocked
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 only allows waiting in the box if your exit road itself is clear.

questions.question: Who else needs similar wide clearance and slow passing speeds under Rule 163 / 215?
options: Horse riders and pedestrians walking in the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 gives wide, slow clearance to cyclists, horse riders, and walkers.

questions.question: When you stop in a queue behind another car, how much space should you leave?
options: Enough to see their rear tyres on the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 and queueing advice keep space to steer around if needed.

questions.question: When pulling away from the side of the road, when should you signal?
options: Before you pull away, if other road users could benefit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 advises signalling in good time when pulling away.

questions.question: Why should you often drive slower than the speed limit?
options: Roadworks, rain, bends, or parked cars can make the limit unsafe
Because speed limits are just suggestions
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 and 125 state the limit is a maximum, not a target.

questions.question: Why must you NEVER drive anti-clockwise around a roundabout?
options: You would drive head-on into oncoming circulating traffic
It wears out the left tyres
It is allowed only for emergency vans
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 prevents head-on collisions by keeping all traffic clockwise.

questions.question: When turning left from a side road onto a main road, which direction is the main danger first?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 checks right first for nearside flow, and left for overtaking traffic.

questions.question: When two lanes merge into one, how should you treat a driver alongside you?
options: Leave space and merge in turn safely
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and merging advice promote safe, courteous lane changes.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, does the same give-way-to-the-right rule apply?
options: Yes, give way to traffic from your right just like a full roundabout
Traffic from the left goes first
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and 188 apply the same give-way-to-the-right rule at mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: Why do many drivers drift out of lane on roundabouts?
options: Looking only at the kerb instead of planning their path around the curve
Holding the steering wheel with both hands
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 advises looking ahead along your lane path to hold a clean line.

questions.question: When going straight ahead at a normal two-lane roundabout with no special arrows, which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 recommends the left-hand lane for straight ahead unless signs direct otherwise.

questions.question: If the traffic light is green but the exit past the box is full, what could happen if you enter?
options: You will be stuck in the box when the cross traffic gets a green light
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 prevents drivers getting trapped across live junctions.

questions.question: What phrase helps drivers count two seconds cleanly?
options: Say 'Only a fool breaks the two-second rule'
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 suggests a steady two-second count past a fixed landmark.

questions.question: Why should you check that your indicator has cancelled after a gentle bend?
options: Self-cancelling switches may not turn off after a small steer
It is required only on motorways
Indicators turn off after two flashes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds you to cancel signals manually if they stay on.

questions.question: What tells you a 20 mph zone has ended?
options: A sign showing the new limit, such as 30
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 requires following the signed limit until a new limit sign appears.

questions.question: If the roundabout is completely clear to your right, must you still stop?
options: No, keep moving smoothly if it is safe and clear
Yes, stop for three seconds every time
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 requires giving way, not stopping unnecessarily when the way is clear.

questions.question: When turning right at a small mini-roundabout, what mistake do learners sometimes make?
options: Cutting the corner on the wrong side of the white circle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 warn drivers not to cut across the wrong side of the central marking.

questions.question: Why is a right signal on approach helpful to drivers waiting at the left-hand entrance?
options: It warns them you are staying on the roundabout past their exit
It tells them to pull out in front of you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 helps waiting drivers judge whether you will cross their path.

questions.question: You are in the right-hand lane of a two-lane roundabout and want to exit. What must you check before signalling left and moving out?
options: Your left mirror and blind spot for vehicles on your left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires checking left before moving across to exit.

questions.question: Why must you watch the outer lane carefully when joining a two-lane roundabout?
options: A driver in the inner lane might switch outward or a cyclist might be riding there
The outer lane is always closed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 advises watching all circulating lanes and cyclists before entering.

questions.question: What should you do if temporary roadworks traffic lights are stuck on red for a long time?
options: Wait and check if they are faulty before moving only with extreme care
questions.explain: Rule 176: never assume a red light is broken quickly; only proceed with extreme caution if clearly failed.

questions.question: What if the first exit is straight ahead and there is no left turn?
options: Treat it as straight ahead and do not signal on approach unless signs show left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 matches your signal to the road layout and signs.

questions.question: After you have entered the exit road from a roundabout, what should you do?
options: Check your left signal has cancelled
Leave the left signal on for 300 metres
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require cancelling your signal once clear.

questions.question: When you are stopped in a queue, where should you wait if space ends at a zebra crossing?
options: Before the stripes so the crossing stays clear
On top of the black and white stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 and 192 keep crossings clear for people on foot.

questions.question: At a tiny mini-roundabout with little space, should you still signal your turn?
options: Yes, signal clearly in good time before entering
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and 188 still require clear approach signals at mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, why can it be hard to give a separate left exit signal?
options: The junction is very small, so keep your focus on steering safely if tight
Left signals are banned at mini-roundabouts
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 188 note there is less time to signal exit at very small mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: May you overtake a parked car that broke down on the zig-zags? Only if safe?
options: Wait if unsure, and pass slowly only if it is clearly stationary and broken down, watching for pedestrians
Never pass a broken-down car even after checking
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids overtaking moving or stopped-for-crossing lead vehicles; pass broken-down obstructions only with extreme care.
